name: Macro photography
means: Extreme magnification: the subject fills the frame, the plane of sharp focus is a few millimetres deep, everything in front of and behind it dissolves to smooth colour, and surface micro-texture the eye never sees becomes the subject.
prose: a macro photograph at life-size magnification, the subject filling the frame, a plane of sharp focus only millimetres deep with everything in front and behind dissolved to smooth colour, visible surface micro-texture and dust, soft diffused ring light, dark uncluttered surround
negative_add: wide shot, deep focus, everything in focus, sharp background, scenery, illustration, anime
works_for: video poorly. At this magnification a millimetre of drift is half the frame and LTX has nothing stable to hold onto, so the subject swims. Inferred.
note: Strong because it is the depth-of-field lever - which studio/tags/depth_of_field.json rates the most reliable lens control in the project - pushed to its end stop. It inherits that card's grammar warning: declaring a dissolved background and then asking for background detail or scenery anywhere in the same prompt cancels both and you get an ordinary photograph. Give it a real noun to magnify - a housefly's eye, a rusted bolt thread, frost along a leaf edge - because at this magnification the whole picture IS the surface, and a vague subject leaves the model nothing to texture. Unavailable on the anime checkpoint: `object focus, close-up` there gives a drawn close-up, not magnification. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Tightened the crop but produced no macro optics - no extreme shallow plane, no change in subject scale. The frame is a portrait, not a macro.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py
